title: Almost invariant functions at generic groupoid orbits
statement: Let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid scheme [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Assume $s,t$ are finite and of finite presentation [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $x\in U$ write $O(x)=t(s^{-1}(\{x\}))$ for its orbit; arrows can be compared and composed after extending their residue fields to a common field. Let $x_1,\ldots,x_m\in U$, with $m\geq0$, have orbits consisting of generic points [def-sc-generic-point] of irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $U$. Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $j:U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be an immersion [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal such that $j(U)\cap V(I)=\varnothing$ and $V(I)\cup j(U)$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Then there is $h\in I$ for which $j^{-1}D(h)$ is an affine open subscheme containing every $x_i$ and satisfying $s^{-1}(j^{-1}D(h))=t^{-1}(j^{-1}D(h))$. Here $V(I)$ is the set of prime ideals containing $I$ and $D(h)$ the set of primes not containing $h$.

proof.text: If $m=0$, take $h=0\in I$: its inverse-image principal open is empty, hence affine (the spectrum of the zero ring), and both inverse images under $s,t$ are empty. Henceforth $m>0$.

The structure map of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is separated by lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated. Composing it with the immersion $j$ is separated by lem-trf-immersion-over-separated-base, so $U$ is quasi-separated by lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated. Apply lem-sfb-finite-groupoid-generic-affine-flat-thickening with the given finite-presentation hypotheses and generic orbits. Obtain invariant affine $V\subseteq U$ and an invariant affine thickening $V'\hookrightarrow V$ of finite presentation containing the marked points, with restricted source and target finite locally free. Write $B=\Gamma(V',\mathcal O_{V'})$.

source.place: Tag 0ABF (lemma-find-almost-invariant-function), first sentence: invariant affine pair from Tag 0ABC

proof.text: Put $C=V(I)\cup j(U)$, closed by hypothesis. The subspace $j(U)=C\setminus V(I)$ is open in $C$, and $j$ is a homeomorphism onto its image. Thus $j(V)$ is open in $C$ and $Z=C\setminus j(V)=V(I)\cup j(U\setminus V)$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Choose its vanishing ideal $K$ and put $J=I\cap K$. Since $V(I)\subseteq Z$, the prime-ideal identity $V(I\cap K)=V(I)\cup V(K)$ gives $V(J)=Z$. Consequently $J\subseteq I$, $j(V)\cap V(J)=\varnothing$, and $V(J)\cup j(V)=C$. These same assertions hold for $j(V')=j(V)$.

source.place: Tag 0ABF (lemma-find-almost-invariant-function), boundary ideal J, with closedness and containment written out

proof.text: Every orbit of a marked point is finite, since $s$ has finite fibres. Let $F$ be their finite union. Invariance of $V$ puts $F$ inside $V$. The arrows restricted to $V'$ have the same underlying points as the arrows restricted to $V$: the ideals pulled back from the thickening vanish in every residue field, hence their sum does also. Thus the restricted orbits are the original ones. For each $y\in F$, its image prime $\mathfrak p_{j(y)}$ does not contain $J$, since $j(y)\notin V(J)$. Prime avoidance gives $f\in J$ outside all these primes. Hence the restriction $b=j^\sharp(f)\in B$ is nonzero at every point of every marked orbit.

source.place: Tag 0ABF (lemma-find-almost-invariant-function), choice of f by Algebra Tag 00DS

proof.text:
The arrow scheme $R'$ is affine because $s'$ is finite and $V'$ is affine. Form $g=N_{s'}(t'{}^\sharp(b))\in B$ using lem-pd-finite-locally-free-norm-charts. By lem-a1-affine-groupoid-invariant-norm, $s'{}^\sharp(g)=t'{}^\sharp(g)$, so $D_{V'}(g)$ is invariant. On each finite-free chart the norm-prime criterion says $g(y)
e0$ exactly when $b(t'(r))
e0$ for every point $r$ above $y$ under $s'$. Our choice of $f$ therefore gives $g(x_i)
e0$. The identity arrow at any $y$ is one of these points, so $g(y)
e0$ implies $b(y)
e0$: $D_{V'}(g)\subseteq D_{V'}(b)$. This also covers nonreduced fibres and varying local rank.

source.place: Tag 0ABF (lemma-find-almost-invariant-function), norm and determinant trick, with the nonvanishing test made explicit

proof.text: Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be induced by $j|_{V'}$, so $b=\varphi(f)$ and $(V')_b=(j|_{V'})^{-1}D_A(f)$. The morphism $(V')_b\to D_A(f)$ is an immersion: write $j$ as a closed immersion $U\to O$ followed by an open $O\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$. Since $j$ is a homeomorphism onto its image, $j(V)=j(U)\cap O_1$ for an open $O_1\subseteq O$, so $V\to O\cap O_1$ is a closed immersion (both defining conditions are local on the target). With the closed immersion $V'\to V$ this gives a closed immersion $V'\to O\cap O_1$ by lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp; restrict it over $O\cap O_1\cap D_A(f)$ and follow it by the open immersion into $D_A(f)$. Its image is $C\cap D_A(f)$, since $f\in J$ vanishes on $V(J)$ and $C=V(J)\cup j(V')$. It is closed. Hence the morphism is a closed immersion by lem-weil-pbc-immersion-closed-image-closed-immersion. Its affine description gives a surjection $A_f\to B_b$, using the principal-open section formula. Lift $g/1\in B_b$ to $a/f^k$ with $a\in A$, $k\geq0$. Equality of fractions gives some $\ell\geq0$ with $b^\ell(\varphi(a)-b^kg)=0$ in $B$. Thus $\varphi(f^\ell a)=b^{k+\ell}g$. Set $h=f^{\ell+1}a\in J\subseteq I$ and $n=k+\ell+1>0$. Then $\varphi(h)=b^ng$, and $D_A(h)\subseteq D_A(f)$.

source.place: Tag 0ABF (lemma-find-almost-invariant-function), clearing denominators in f^n g, retaining the possible localization kernel

proof.text: Let $W=j^{-1}D_A(h)$. Since $h\in J$ and $V(J)$ contains $j(U\setminus V)$, $W\subseteq V$. On $V'$, the equality $\varphi(h)=b^ng$ gives $W\cap V'=D_{V'}(b)\cap D_{V'}(g)=D_{V'}(g)$ by the inclusion proved above. The thickening identifies $|V'|=|V|$, and the arrow thickening identifies $|R'|=|R_V|$. Therefore the invariance of $D_{V'}(g)$ gives $s^{-1}(W)=t^{-1}(W)$ on $R_V$. Outside $R_V$ neither endpoint lies in $V$, by invariance of $V$, so the equality holds on all $R$. Equal underlying opens have equal open subschemes. The marked points belong to $W$. Finally $W$ is the principal open of the restriction of $j^\sharp(h)$ on the affine scheme $V$, hence is affine by lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime. This proves every assertion on the original $U$, without changing its scheme structure.
